text:
ConocoPhillips ticked up 0.59% to $135.05 today as oil prices surged on escalating U.S.-Iran tensions in the Middle East. Reports of Iranian attacks on U.S. Navy ships pushed crude oil toward $99 a barrel—a 6-week high—and energy companies like ConocoPhillips benefit when oil prices rise, since higher crude translates directly to stronger margins and revenue for producers.

The stock remains up modestly over two weeks despite the volatility of the last few trading days, reflecting how geopolitical risk in the Middle East supports energy sector strength. With the Strait of Hormuz—a critical chokepoint for global oil shipping—at the center of U.S.-Iran tensions, any disruption to supply keeps upward pressure on prices and supports oil majors' profitability.
